decisionsTitle: Each person waiting sees where they stand in the line, and the event page says how many wait (amending §348, §587, §612, §615)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01**, in his own words. He asked: «Acum mai am nevoie de încă o setare cu "lista de așteptare e publică"». The dispatcher asked what that meant, and he answered two of its three options: «Fiecare își vede locul» and «Doar numărul, pe pagina evenimentului» (the third, «Setare pe eveniment: lista de așteptare publică», is the sibling branch `feat/waiting-list-public-switch`, not this one). He then narrowed the first: «E ok să aștepte, ei nu vor afla când s-au înscris restul pe listă și noi putem alege pe cine să luăm din listă».

**The rule as built.** Each person waiting is told where they stand **only while the event's `waitlist_auto_offer` is true**, because then a freed place really goes in order. With it false — the club chooses whom to offer a place, so nobody learns when the rest of the line registered — the person is told only **how many others wait and that the club chooses**: no position, no length of the line as a place in it. And the event page says how many wait. Nothing here makes the list of names more public.

### What happened until now

A person on the waiting list was told they were «Pe lista de așteptare» and nothing else: not how long the line was, nor how far they were from the front. The registration's own page showed no state at all for a single registration (only a family's card has the state chip), «Toate înscrierile mele» showed the chip, and the `WAITLIST_JOINED` email said «te-am adăugat pe lista de așteptare. Te vom anunța dacă se eliberează un loc.» The event page said how many wait in some states and not in others: «3 pe lista de așteptare» as a line of its own when places were free, «… — 3 așteaptă deja un loc» in the full state's lead, and nothing at all on the places line (§615: «150 înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare»), nor when the line was full or the event kept none.

### The decision

**A. Where a person stands.** With `waitlist_auto_offer` true: «Ești pe locul 3 din 10 persoane de pe lista de așteptare.» and «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» With it false: «Ești pe lista de așteptare, împreună cu alte 9 persoane. Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» (alone in the line, in either reading: «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» and then the setting's sentence, never «locul 1 din 1 persoană»). It appears in three places, from one reader:
1. **The registration's own page** (`/registrations/manage/<token>`): under the state — a one-person page gets the state's words as a heading, «Pe lista de așteptare», which it never had, and the sentence under it; a family's card has the state chip, so only the sentence.
2. **«Toate înscrierile mele»**: the same sentence on a `WAITLISTED` row, under the date.
3. **The `WAITLIST_JOINED` email**: with offers in order, «Când am trimis acest email, erai pe locul 3 din 10.» / "When we sent this email, you were number 3 of 10."; with the club choosing, no position: «Când am trimis acest email, pe lista de așteptare mai așteptau alte 9 persoane.» / "When we sent this email, 9 other people were on the waiting list." (alone, in either reading: «… erai singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.») — one sentence added after the body, in both halves, worded as of the moment of rendering because an email is read later and the line moves. Never «ești» in an email. It is a machine-added sentence after the body whoever wrote it, like the other facts of a send (§547, §588): a club that rewrote the message's words still sends it.

**One reader, the allocator's order.** `readWaitlistPosition(db, registrationId)` in `registrations/repository.ts` returns `{ position, length, autoOffer }`, or null when the registration is not `WAITLISTED`; it still computes the position whatever the setting — the surfaces decide whether to say it — but is null on a cancelled event. The position is `row_number() over (order by waitlisted_at asc, id asc)` among the event's `WAITLISTED` rows — `lockOldestWaitlisted`'s own order, the one the allocator offers places in, written as a window over the same rows rather than as a second statement of the rule — and the length is the count of those rows. An offered person (`WAITLIST_OFFERED`) has left the line; a cancelled or expired row never was; `kind` appears in no condition, so a `TEST` row stands in the line like a real one (`AGENTS.md` §12.6), as `countEligibleWaitlisted` counts it. Two statements, no lock: a number one place stale the instant it renders is the same as the public counts, and nothing is decided from it. `listManagedPeople` and `listActiveRegistrationsForParticipant` carry it (`waitlistStanding`) on a waiting row only, one read each; a row that is not waiting costs nothing.

**The position follows the setting (§615).** `autoOffer` — the event's «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» as it stands when the page is read or the email rendered, from the same read of the event row, so no surface makes a second query — decides what is said. On «Da» the position and «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.»; on «Nu» the count of others and «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.», and the position is not in the page's markup at all: the owner decided that with offers handed out by hand nobody learns the order. The email is as of the moment it was rendered and says the same in its own register, with or without a position.

**Alone, and on a cancelled event (round 3).** A person alone in the line reads «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» followed by the setting's sentence («Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» or «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.»), and the email says the same alone in both readings; «locul 1 din 1 persoană» is no longer said anywhere. On a **cancelled event** (`events.event_status = CANCELLED`) none of the three surfaces says a sentence about the line: a cancellation keeps every registration in its state (§331.6) and `fillAvailableSpots` offers nothing (§331.7), so «Ești pe locul 2 din 5 … Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» would promise what will not happen, and the page already says the event is cancelled. `readWaitlistPosition` returns null for a cancelled event — from the event row it already joins for `autoOffer`, no extra query — so the three surfaces skip the sentence (and the one-person page's state heading, which was only there to carry it) by the same rule, the email at render time. The registration itself is untouched.

**The words.** `Registrations.waitlist` in both catalogues: `position.{one,few,other}` through `countForm` on the line's length («din 1 persoană», «din 10 persoane», «din 20 de persoane»; English repeats its one form under the three keys), `others.{one,few,other}` through `countForm` on the number of others («cu o altă persoană», «cu alte 9 persoane», «cu alte 20 de persoane»; English «with 1 other», «with 9 others»), `alone` (also with offers in order, when the line is one), `orderAuto`, `orderClub`; `position.one` («din 1 persoană») is no longer reachable and stays only because the form is looked up by `countForm`. The email's words are in `templates.ts` as every email's are, through `countForm` and no ICU plural. No number is typed in code.

**The email reads the line at render time, and why.** The renderer already has the database and the registration the outbox row names (`registrationId`), as it has for every other fact of a send (`render.ts`); the template itself has none. A number written into the payload at queue time would be as old as the queueing — and an email is rendered at send time, again at every retry, and again on a staff resend, each after the line moved — so the payload carries nothing new and the sentence is «as of the moment I was rendered» — the setting is read then too. When the person is no longer waiting at render time (an offer was made, they cancelled) or the event is cancelled, the sentence is simply absent.

**Privacy.** The sentence is on the registration's own token page and in its own email, and says numbers about the line and nothing about anybody else: no name, no state of another person; with the club choosing, not even this person's own place. The public list is not touched (`StartList.tsx`, §396, §613): it still shows no position.

**B. The event page says how many wait.** The places line (`fillPhrase`) gains a last part, «10 pe lista de așteptare» ("10 on the waiting list"), whenever anybody waits: «150 de înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 de confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare, 10 pe lista de așteptare». The number is `readPublicPlaces`'s `waitlisted` — the `WAITLISTED` rows with no offer yet, from the same count the door already reads and the public cache carries, with no second query; a test registration stands in it as in every public count (and cannot exist in production). It rides on `PublicFill` (`waitlisted`, set by `publicFill`, absent when nobody waits and in a cache entry from before the halves were counted). It reuses the existing `cta.waitingCount` words.

**Not twice in one card.** Each state of the page says the number once:
- **Open, with a places line** (a capped event): the places line carries it, and the separate «N pe lista de așteptare» line it used to have beneath the free-place count (§587, §612) is gone — the same words, moved into the line where the other counts are. **The order on the page changes with it:** the people waiting are now said on the places line, and the open offer's own line («N loc oferit din lista de așteptare», §612) follows it, so the event page reads waiting, then offered, where the listing card (`openLinePhrases`, which has no places line) still reads offered, then waiting. The two are the same words and the same counts in a different order; the card is not touched, and the order is not worth a second places-line part for the offer — the places line is the page's total, the offered line is its detail. SPECS: BR-REQ-035-01 criterion 14 (order «after the free places … then pe lista de așteptare») and BR-REQ-034-01 criteria 15–16 (the places line's «three parts») are amended in the same landing. An uncapped event has no places line and no waiting list, so nothing changes there.
- **Full, the line takes people:** the lead already says «… — 3 așteaptă deja un loc.» (§587, the owner's words of 2026-09-30), the places line leaves it out (`fillPhrase(…, { withWaiting: false })`), so the card does not say the same number in two registers. The lead's count is the whole line (waiting plus an open offer), as it was.
- **The line full, or no list at all** (a sentence and no button): there is no lead with a number, so the places line says it.
- **The listing card** (`CardRegistration`) has no places line and was already consistent: the open state's detail carries the offered and the waiting counts (`openLinePhrases`), the full state's lead the count. Unchanged.

### Rejected
- **A position on the public list.** The list shows the confirmed, and — behind the notice (§396) — the ticked pending and waiting, each with its state and no position; a position beside a name is a disclosure the privacy notice does not describe. Not touched.
- **A position written into the email's payload at queue time.** Stale at the first retry; see above.
- **A promise of order in the email.** The setting can change before the email is read; the email says only what the line was when it was rendered.
- **The position whatever the setting.** The first version of this branch told everybody their place and said, for the club's choice, that the club chooses; the owner's narrowing («ei nu vor afla când s-au înscris restul pe listă») makes the place itself the thing withheld.
- **A second count query for the event page.** `waitlisted` is already in the cached read.
- **A new setting for any of this.** None needed: the sentence follows the setting that exists.

### Consequences
`registrations/repository.ts` (`readWaitlistPosition`, null on a cancelled event); `registrations/domain/waitlist-standing.ts` (the type); `registrations/ui/waitlist-position-words.ts` (the two readings of the setting); `registrations/manage-family.ts` and `registrations/my-registrations.ts` (`waitlistStanding`); the two token pages; `notifications/render.ts` and `templates.ts` (`waitlistStanding`, `waitlistPosition`); `events/domain/registration-cta.ts` (`PublicFill.waitlisted`), `events/ui/counted-phrases.ts` (`fillPhrase`), `RegistrationCta.tsx`, `registration-door.ts`; `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Registrations.waitlist`). The allocator, the capacity formula, `waitlist.ts` and the public list are untouched. No migration, no dependency. Tests: `unit/registrations/waitlist-standing-words.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/waitlist-position.test.ts`, `integration/notifications/waitlist-joined-position.test.ts` (new; the cancelled event on the page, «Toate înscrierile mele» and the email), `unit/events/counted-phrases.test.ts`, `unit/events/registration-cta.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/registration-fill-render.test.ts`.
changelogLine: - **«Ești pe locul 3 din 10 persoane de pe lista de așteptare»** — while the event offers freed places in order, each person waiting sees their place in the line on their own page, in «Toate înscrierile mele» and, as of the moment it was sent, in the waiting-list email; while the club chooses whom to offer a place, they see only how many others wait and that the club chooses, never a position; the event page's places line ends with how many wait. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a registration on the waiting list of an event whose «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» is on, when its own page (the manage link) or «Toate înscrierile mele» is opened, then under its state it says «Ești pe locul {n} din {m} persoane de pe lista de așteptare.» / "You are number {n} of {m} on the waiting list." — {n} is 1 plus the `WAITLISTED` registrations of the event ahead in the allocator's own order (`waitlisted_at`, then `id`) and {m} every `WAITLISTED` registration of the event, from one reader (`readWaitlistPosition`); Romanian's three forms through `countForm` on {m}; a one-person page shows the state's words as a heading above it; alone in the line it reads «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare. Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» rather than «locul 1 din 1 persoană»; a registration that is not waiting, or whose event is cancelled (no offer will go out, §331), shows no such sentence; an offered, cancelled or expired registration is not in the line, a `TEST` registration is, and the sentence names nobody else (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

While the event's «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» is on, the sentence adds «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» / "Freed places are offered in order."; while it is off the page says no position and no length as a place: «Ești pe lista de așteptare, împreună cu alte {m−1} persoane. Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» / "You are on the waiting list, with {m−1} others. The club chooses whom to offer a freed place." — Romanian's forms through `countForm` on {m−1} («cu o altă persoană», «cu alte 9 persoane», «cu alte 20 de persoane»), and «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» followed by the same setting's sentence when {m} is 1, with offers in order too; the setting is read as it stands when the page is opened (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The places line of the event page — in every state that shows it — ends with «{n} pe lista de așteptare» / "{n} on the waiting list" whenever anybody is `WAITLISTED` (`readPublicPlaces`'s `waitlisted`, the cached count the door already reads, no further query, a test registration counted as in every public count), after the confirmed, in-progress and kept parts: «150 de înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 de confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare, 10 pe lista de așteptare»; with nobody waiting the line is as it was; the number is said once in a card — in the full state the lead's «… — {n} așteaptă deja un loc.» carries it and the places line leaves it out, and the open state's separate «{n} pe lista de așteptare» line is the places line's part (amends criterion 11); it also amends BR-REQ-035-01 criterion 14 and BR-REQ-034-01 criteria 15 and 16: on the event page the places line, with the waiting count as its last part, comes first, and the open offer's «{n} loc oferit din lista de așteptare» line follows it, where the listing card (no places line) still says the offer, then the waiting; the places line may have a fourth part, the people waiting, after the three of criterion 16 (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The position a waiting person is told is the order the allocator offers places in. With `waitlist_auto_offer` on: given three waiting registrations, the one with the earliest `waitlisted_at` reads «locul 1», a tie on the instant is broken by stable id, and when the person ahead is offered a place the next one reads «locul 1» at the next opening of the page. With it off: each of the three reads how many others wait («cu alte 2 persoane») and that the club chooses, and none reads a position (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a `WAITLIST_JOINED` message, when it renders, then after its body — whoever wrote it — it adds one sentence in each half's own language, worded as of the moment of rendering, never as a present state: with the event's «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» on, «Când am trimis acest email, erai pe locul {n} din {m}.» / "When we sent this email, you were number {n} of {m}."; with it off, no position — «Când am trimis acest email, pe lista de așteptare mai așteptau alte {m−1} persoane.» / "When we sent this email, {m−1} other people were on the waiting list." (Romanian's forms through `countForm`; «… erai singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» when {m} is 1, with offers in order too); the numbers and the setting are read at render time from the same reader as the registration's own page with the registration the outbox row names (not from the payload, so a retry or a resend says the line as it is then); nothing is added once the registration is no longer waiting or the event is cancelled (render time), nor to any other message, and no other person is named (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: each person on the waiting list sees where they stand; the places line says how many wait
